# Spec: macos-case-guard
<!-- Generated by /hefesto:hef.spec -->
<!-- Date: 2026-11-16 -->
<!-- Board item: HEF-55 — the macOS static guard refuses a `case` inside a command substitution -->
<!-- req-coverage: scoped -->

## Overview

macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 ends a command substitution `$( … )` at the first `)` of a `case` pattern written
inside it, so the script fails to parse ("syntax error near unexpected token `newline'"). On PR #212
(HEF-22) such a `case` in `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (`fg_pushrw="$( … case … esac … )"`, fixed in
`8365d75` by moving the body into `fg_pushrw_list()`) passed shellcheck and the suite's macOS portability
guard (`tests/smoke.sh`, block "macOS portability", rule 1 — a per-line regex) and failed 187 smoke cases
on the Mac runner. This feature adds a rule to that static guard: a `case` inside an open `$(` in
`hooks/*.sh` or `install.sh` is reported on Linux, before it reaches a Mac. The guard is checked against
fixtures, and a mutation of the guard must turn the suite red.

## Decisions (made here, from the code — no clarification needed)

- **D1 — a nesting-aware scan, not another line regex.** The offending form spans lines (the HEF-22 case
  sat three lines into a multi-line `$(`), and seven lines on today's tree hold `$(` and `case` on the same
  line with the substitution already closed (e.g. `hooks/lane-guard.sh:31`, `hooks/session-launch.sh:131`,
  `hooks/status-board.sh:37,450`, `hooks/ledger-automerge.sh:227`, `hooks/session-launch.sh:355`,
  `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:412`). A regex on one line cannot tell them apart; a scan that tracks
  whether a `$(` is still open when the word `case` is read can. It reads the file as bash does closely
  enough for this rule: comments, single-quoted text and the literal text of double-quoted strings do
  not count; `$((` arithmetic is not a command substitution; a `(`…`)` group or array assignment nests
  without being a substitution.
- **D2 — every `case` inside an open `$(` is reported**, including the `case x in (pat)` leading-paren
  form. The remedy is one shape for all of them — a function the substitution calls, the form
  `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:334` documents — and a rule with an exception the Linux CI cannot exercise is
  a rule nobody can trust. A `case` in a function body is not inside a `$(` even when the function is
  called from one, so it passes.
- **D3 — scope is the guard's existing file set**, `hooks/*.sh` and `install.sh`. Backtick substitutions
  are out of scope (the hooks do not use them for multi-line bodies; the item names `$(`…`)`).
- **D4 — the guard lives in the suite**, beside rule 1 of the "macOS portability" block in
  `tests/smoke.sh`, as a function that takes file paths, so the same code runs over the real files and
  the fixtures. No hook changes: today's tree has no `case` inside a `$(` (HEF-22 removed the only one),
  and the rule must report nothing on it.
- **D5 — fixtures are `.txt` files under `tests/fixtures/`** (not `.sh`: the commit gate runs `bash -n`
  on staged `.sh` files, and the failing fixture is a bash 3.2 syntax error by design): one holding the HEF-22 shape (a multi-line `$(`
  with a `case` in it) and one-line variant, which the guard must report; one holding the passing shapes
  (the function form, and `$(`…`)` followed by `case` on one line), which it must not.

## User Scenarios

### US1: A `case` inside a command substitution is reported [P1]
- **Given** a hook file containing `x="$(` on one line, a `case … in pat) … ;; esac` on a later line, and
  the closing `)"` after it
- **When** the suite's macOS portability block runs
- **Then** it reports a failure naming the file and the line of the `case`, and says why (bash 3.2 ends
  the substitution at the pattern's `)`) and the remedy (move it into a function)
- **Edge**: the `case` and the `$(` share one line (`v="$(case "$a" in x) echo 1 ;; esac)"`) — still reported
- **Edge**: a `$(` nested inside another `$(` holds the `case` — still reported
- **Negative**: the report is a failure of the block, never a warning the block passes over

### US2: The function form and a closed substitution pass [P1]
- **Given** a function whose body holds a `case`, called as `x="$(the_function)"`, and lines where a
  `$(` closes before a `case` begins on the same line (`t="$(readlink "$p")"; case "$t" in /*) … esac`)
- **When** the guard scans the file
- **Then** it reports nothing
- **Edge**: the word `case` in a comment, in single quotes, or in the text of a double-quoted string
  inside a `$(` (`$(echo "in case of")`) — not reported
- **Edge**: `$(( … ))` arithmetic followed by a `case` — not reported
- **Edge**: a `case` whose branch opens a `$(` (`case "$l" in /*) d="$(dirname "$l")" ;; esac`) — not reported

### US3: Today's tree is clean, and the guard is proven to fire [P1]
- **Given** the repository at this change
- **When** tier 1 of `tests/smoke.sh` runs
- **Then** the guard reports nothing over `hooks/*.sh` and `install.sh`, reports every case in the
  failing fixture, reports nothing in the passing fixture, and the block's `ok` line names the new rule
- **Error case**: a mutation that disables the `case` detection (or the `$(` tracking) in a copy of the
  guard makes the failing fixture pass — the suite must report "mutation survived" as a failure
- **Negative**: the fixtures are not part of the scanned set (`hooks/*.sh`, `install.sh`), so the
  failing fixture never turns the real-tree check red

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Scenario |
|----|-------------|----------|----------|
| FR-001 | The macOS portability block of `tests/smoke.sh` fails when a file in `hooks/*.sh` or `install.sh` has the word `case` (as a command) while a `$(` command substitution is open, across lines or on one line, nested or not | P1 | US1 |
| FR-002 | The failure names file and line of each offending `case`, the bash 3.2 reason, and the remedy (a function called from the substitution) | P1 | US1 |
| FR-003 | A `case` in a function body called from a substitution, a `case` after a substitution closed on the same line, a `$(` opened inside a `case` branch, and `$((` arithmetic are not reported | P1 | US2 |
| FR-004 | The word `case` in a comment, single-quoted text, or the literal text of a double-quoted string is not reported | P1 | US2 |
| FR-005 | The guard is one function taking file paths; the block runs it over `hooks/*.sh` + `install.sh` and over fixtures under `tests/fixtures/` — a failing fixture (HEF-22 multi-line shape, one-line shape, nested shape) whose every `case` must be reported, a passing fixture that must report nothing, and a desync fixture on which the guard must say it lost sync (a scanner that stopped reading never reads as clean) | P1 | US3 |
| FR-006 | On today's tree the guard reports nothing over `hooks/*.sh` and `install.sh` | P1 | US3 |
| FR-007 | At least one mutation of the guard (disable `case` detection; ignore `$(` depth) is applied to a copy and must make the failing fixture go unreported; a surviving mutation, or a mutation that did not apply, fails the block | P1 | US3 |
| FR-008 | The block's `ok` line names the new rule and the mutation count; a `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry records the guard under HEF-55 | P2 | US3 |

## Success Criteria

| ID | Criterion | Validation Method |
|----|-----------|-------------------|
| SC-001 | Fails before, passes after: with the guard function's `case` detection removed, the fixture check fails; with it, tier 1 passes | Run `tests/smoke.sh` tier 1 on the change, and on a copy with the detection stubbed out |
| SC-002 | Reverting `8365d75` in a scratch copy of `hooks/hefesto-setup.sh` (the inline `fg_pushrw="$( … case … )"`) is reported by the guard | Guard function run on the reverted copy |
| SC-003 | Zero reports over today's `hooks/*.sh` and `install.sh` (no false positives on the seven same-line `$(`/`case` lines) | Tier 1 `ok` line for "macOS portability" |
| SC-004 | Tier 1 total failures stay 0; no file outside `tests/smoke.sh`, `tests/fixtures/`, `CHANGELOG.md` changes | `tests/smoke.sh`; `git diff --stat` |

## Clarifications
_None — the decisions above settle every open point from the code._
